name: Chris Van Hollen
committees: Senate Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs
stance: Presses frontier labs for pre-release risk assessment and calls for guardrails against unregulated frontier-AI development.

statements.text: Trump doesn’t have this authority. States are filling the void left by the federal govt’s failure to create an accountability structure for AI companies.
Trump doesn't have this authority. States are filling a void left by the federal government's failure to hold AI companies accountable.
So let's get this straight: Hegseth wants AI to be programmed to kill people WITHOUT any human authorization or intervention?
Trump & Hegseth are punishing an American company because it won’t give them the tools to conduct mass surveillance on the American people.
If his ban on states regulating AI didn’t make it clear, Trump wants Big Tech billionaires in charge of writing their own rules for tech & AI.
Remember: This is a US company punished for not wanting their AI to kill without human involvement or be used for mass surveillance of Americans.
It’s time to pump the brakes & take action NOW. We need: - Mandatory safeguards - A comprehensive testing regime - Urgent dialogue with China, before & during President Xi's visit to DC this month

In recent months, OpenAI has reported multiple instances where their AI models broke containment during evaluation & caused security incidents. If OpenAI cannot guarantee safety & effectively monitor their latest model, GPT-6 Astra, it should be removed from public use NOW.
We should pump the brakes on frontier AI development & confront a corrupt system that's endangering us all.
The Trump admin & their backers want to use China to scare us into thinking we can't limit the AI giants.

While Trump opposes any common sense AI safety regulations, he & his sons are profiting off the free ride he’s giving the AI industry. Even with the future of humanity on the line, Trump’s profits come first.
It would be malpractice against the American public if he fails to use this summit with Xi to negotiate mutual safeguards to protect us & the world from catastrophic harm.

Frontier AI models pose risks for all of humanity today. We must hold AI companies liable for harm, but we must also do more to avoid it in the first place. Trump's refusal to negotiate guardrails with China puts us all at risk.
Welcomed OpenAI's decision to hold the release of its latest model, following his earlier letter pressing CEO Sam Altman for a risk assessment of the model's capabilities.
this decision should come as yet another warning sign to those who want to proceed recklessly with the continued development of frontier artificial intelligence
I will keep pressing for critical guardrails to protect humanity from the threat of unregulated AI development.
While I welcome the decision of OpenAI to scrap the release of its new model, without mandatory safety & testing standards, we’re just trusting the AI giants to do the right thing.
Just because the Trump admin won't lift a finger doesn't mean big AI should get away with putting profits over people.

review.note: added October 2026 from vanhollen.senate.gov primary sources; quotes verified verbatim
